speaker: Doctor
text: That lacy, reticular rash sparing the mouth is very characteristic. Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling in your fingers or wrists recently? Also, do you recall being in an area where mosquitoes are common, or did you have any tick bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a classic presentation; have you noticed any significant joint pain or stiffness in her fingers, wrists, or ankles recently? Also, has anyone she lives with been recently diagnosed with a similar rash or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The combination of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, along with mild fever and headache, is highly characteristic of this viral illness. While I have reached my diagnostic limit of questions, this clinical picture is distinct from other rashes like those in Scarlet Fever or Kawasaki Disease.
